text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Private sector calls for setting up a permanent body to follow up economic policies.
- Cabinet approves suspension of customs duties on the import of rice and sugar for six months to encourage private sector and agrees to the financial protocol to be signed with France.

- Prime Minister Kabariti emphasises the importance of continued contacts between the private and public sectors, recommendation to set up a permanent council to follow up on political and economic legislation.
- Ample supply of foodstuffs for the coming Ramadan (Moslem fasting) month.
- Ministry of Supply to transform phosphate silo into grain storage warehouse.
- King Hussein and French President Chirac to discuss the developments in the peace process and bilateral ties.
- Crown Prince Hassan calls for solving deep-seated problems of the region.
- Prime Minister Kabariti meets Israeli ambassador Shimon Shamir, envoy says progress also reached on trade and transport.
- Start of talks between King Hussein and Chirac on Wednesday evening. The two leaders will discuss developments in the region, the peace process and bilateral ties.
- World Bank to lend Jordan $120 million to expand social safety network.
- In a conference to support the people of Hebron, Palestinian leader Arafat praises King Hussein for his continued support of the Palestinian cause.
